The unusually long three-week gap between the fourth and fifth developer beta versions of macOS has finally been broken — Apple released the fifth version last Monday, and followed up with a sixth version just a week later. Here's what's new.

Apple releases macOS 27 developer beta 6

With the official release date drawing closer, Apple is now pushing the sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate to all developers.

The fifth beta released last week brought new icons for apps like Siri, Chess, and Safari, but otherwise came with no other notable new features (or bug fixes).

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a standalone Siri app, a unified rounded-corner design across all system windows and apps, as well as AI-powered features added to Shortcuts and Safari that let users create extensions and automation with simple commands.

The system also adds a new "pull-to-refresh" gesture to Safari, which many see as an early signal from Apple pushing macOS toward more touch-friendly operation, paving the way for the rumoured touchscreen MacBook Pro.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also substantially improves iPhone Mirroring, letting users resize windows into different aspect ratios — a move also seen as a prelude to the rumoured foldable iPhone Ultra expected to debut next month.

macOS 27 Golden Gate official build: 26A5416b.

How to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here are the steps to install the fifth developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" next to "Beta Updates"
  • From the dropdown menu at the top right, select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta"
  • Click "Done"

Have you found anything new in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments section.
